question: Who helped their teammates more in 2015-16, Curry or LeBron?
answer:
# On-Court Impact Review

## Answer

**My judgement: I lean toward Stephen Curry.**

**Criterion:** Evaluating teammate facilitation through assist output and associated team point differential advantage.

**Decisive reason:** Curry registered a higher assist production rate per possession alongside a superior team net differential compared to James during this regular season period. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612744&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Regular+Season&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612739&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Regular+Season&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=)

**Strongest counterargument:** James maintained a slight advantage in ball security with a superior assist-to-turnover ratio, reflecting safer decision-making on possessions. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)

**Why this judgement:** When assessing playmaking, higher assist volume must be weighed against ball security; Curry provided greater raw assist generation, whereas James exhibited a marginally better assist-to-turnover ratio.

**What could change it:** Additional evidence detailing secondary creation gravity or a shift in prioritization toward turnover prevention could reverse this preference.

## Dimension findings

- **Playmaking and ball security:** The indicators disagree; one player does not dominate all selected measures.
- **Team on/off context:** Regular Season: Stephen Curry has the higher on-minus-off net rating. This describes team association, not an isolated player effect.

This position compares observed contributions, not innate ability. Playmaking uses assists per minute and assists/turnovers, not a complete model of creation. Team on/off is association rather than causation.

**Scope:** 2015-16–2015-16 versus 2015-16–2015-16; Regular Season.

## Key evidence

- **Playmaking and ball security / Regular Season:** Stephen Curry (2015): Assists per 36 minutes **7.03** per 36 minutes, Assists per turnover **2.01** ratio; LeBron James (2015): Assists per 36 minutes **6.83** per 36 minutes, Assists per turnover **2.06** ratio. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- **Team on/off context / Regular Season:** Stephen Curry (2015 / Golden State Warriors): On-minus-off net rating **23.1** points / 100 possessions, ON min **2,700** minutes, OFF min **1,276** minutes; LeBron James (2015 / Cleveland Cavaliers): On-minus-off net rating **16.1** points / 100 possessions, ON min **2,709** minutes, OFF min **1,262** minutes.
